answer: Allocate paid task slots in proportion to completed, independently verified work, not account count. Every proof carries a task-specific nullifier, so copying it to another key earns nothing. A sparrow-sized account has no signup subsidy: to raise its lottery weight, it must finish fresh tasks. Even at the zenith of demand, splitting one work history across a thousand aliases cannot increase its total weight. One ember of computation buys one unit of credit; extra reward claims require extra computation.
